name: Iridescent Materials
visualIdentity: Pearlescent material, flowing silk, or molten glass is the dominant surface. Coherent highlights, controlled color shifts, and a quiet background reveal the finish through measured flow, folds, rotation, or macro framing; avoid rainbow noise and blown reflections.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to macro material studies. Suggested for beauty, fashion, fragrance, and product finish or colorway reveals; can frame editorial or explanatory content when the material supports the story. Interactive HTML suitability is inferred for responsive editorial pages and accessible colorway selectors.
limitations: Keep one dominant finish and one material language per piece. Avoid fast cuts, competing materials, chrome or holographic type, and distracting material motion. Iridescence does not imply physical fluid simulation. Preserve supplied palette and artwork; example colors are optional, reference dependent, and not intrinsic to silk or molten glass.
palette: Optional pearlescent example: background #F1EDEA, foreground #3F4351, accents #A99DC1, #9FB9B2, #D3ADA1. Use discrete tokens; gradients are disabled. Exact task, brand, or reference colors take precedence; do not recolor assets or change semantic roles. Foreground on background contrast is 8.458:1; accent_1 with foreground is 3.882:1 and decorative only for this pairing. Recheck actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Use keyframed deformation or cached simulation with measured flow, folds, rotation, or macro framing. Keep motion coherent and holds readable. For interactive HTML, a colorway selector with accessible radio buttons and visible focus is suggested. A bounded camera orbit is compatible only with real 3D depth; orbit the camera, with keyboard or touch alternatives and a static reduced-motion view. Live pointer/scroll behavior is for interactive delivery; video motion must resolve deterministically from seekable time.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied audio choices. Keep speech intelligible and avoid clipping or competing vocals. Sync and inspect audio with picture; do not infer sound or playback from visual motion.
assetRequirements: Use authored physical materials and nodes for the finish. Blender with bpy and Cycles or EEVEE are suggested for modeling, materials, lighting, animation, and offline rendering; Three.js is an alternative for browser 3D. Prepare suitable fonts and assets locally. Cache or bake stateful simulation, or replay it deterministically; verify repeated, backward, and out-of-order frame requests. Interactive editorial HTML can use prerendered loops or stills, real web fonts, and a poster fallback. Playback controls or waveforms require actual audio assets.
combinations: Style alone suits macro studies. Style-020 editorial typography/layout is suggested for luxury campaigns; keep type color shifts out and background #F1EDEA. Style-096 restrained product motion suits finish and colorway reveals: one move per shot, accents only through material. Keep the dominant finish in either hybrid.
productionApproach: Select renderer and motion engine for visual fidelity and action; use one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the primary video assembly, seekable timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export pipeline. Remotion is only a fallback for unavailability or a verified unmet requirement, with reason recorded. Neither pipeline owns the style rendering. Interactive HTML uses real input behavior; video uses deterministic composition time. Verify representative frames, full playback, dimensions, duration, frame rate, loop continuity, and audio sync.
